newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to import 1.0 mln T soft wheat in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to import 1.0 mln T soft wheat in 1996/97.

text.p: Morocco is forecasting soft wheat imports at around 1.0 million tonnes for the 1996/97 season, including quantities to blend with local wheat which had suffered from bad winter weather, the agriculture ministry said on Wednesday.

"We forecast soft wheat imports for this campaign (1996/97) not to go beyond 10 million quintals (1.0 million tonnes), including quantities to blend wheat which suffered from particular weather conditions this year," the ministry said in a statement.
Morocco received exceptional rains this year, but was also hit by heavy storms in December/January, which led to floods in the north and central areas of the country.
The ministry earlier released figures showing that Morocco harvested 9.75 million tonnes of cereals in 1995/96, beating the previous record of 9.24 million tonnes in the 1993/1994 season.
Analysts said cereals output in 1994/95, hit by severe drought, was around 1.7 million tonnes.
Morocco was also expected to import up to 2.5 million tonnes of soft wheat in the 1995/96 season, they added.
"...The present harvest will enable the country to prepare the next cereal campaign in the best conditions," the ministry said.
It said "this exceptional harvest" coincided with the liberalisation of the cereals sector, but specific measures had been taken by the government to guarantee the marketing of local products.
Four billion dirhams ($465 million) had been devoted by the government, through banks, to cereal traders for the necessary funds.
The average price for purchasing cereals on the local market was set at 245 dirhams per quintal, the ministry added.
